title: Chords: C, F and G Triads
description: The three primary chords of C major as root-position triads in the right hand over single bass roots in the left - the chords behind most beginner songs - held as whole notes, then as half notes.

arrangements.label: Beginner
arrangements.notes: RH plays root-position triads only (1-3-5), the same shape moved to C, F and G, while the LH plays single bass roots (C3 with 5, F3 with 2, G3 with 1); chords change no faster than every half note so the hand always has time to reset.
teachingPoints: Every triad is the same hand shape - thumb, middle finger, little finger on alternate white keys. Learn the shape on C, then slide it to F and G.
RH: C-E-G, F-A-C, G-B-D with 1-3-5. LH plays only the root of each chord: C3 with finger 5, F3 with finger 2, G3 with finger 1 - one fixed hand position covering C3-G3, so the LH never moves.
Play all three notes of a chord at exactly the same instant - listen for one sound, not a roll.
Bars 5-7 change chord every half note (C F | G C | C G): prepare the next shape in the air while the current chord sounds, and keep the beat steady through the change.
